reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a money-making front-running bot and attributes profit to outrunning another trader's transaction and selling in the same block. It directs viewers to install and connect a wallet, deploy the contract, and fund it with at least 0.5 or 1 BNB, while showing a 5 BNB transaction amount. The speaker reports roughly 2.7 BNB in four hours and suggests that larger initial funds can increase results, although a gas-fee loss caveat is included.

citations.quote: Deploy a Frontrun Bot on Pancakeswap and Start making Money
First thing you need to do is to download metamask
we need to head over to remix go on deploy and tran inject web3
Now, we need to top up our contract actually with funds so that we are able to actually, front run any transaction on the mempool
we are using as i said in our case 5 BNB to maximize our profit

opening.argument: The presentation does not conceal downside or present the process as risk-free. It expressly warns that a smaller balance can lose money when gas costs exceed slippage profits, and it limits the contract to Binance Smart Chain rather than implying universal compatibility. The withdrawal step is also described as an available operation after stopping the bot. Those qualifications support a practical, risk-aware demonstration rather than a deceptive promise of certain returns. The speaker's profit example is framed as an observed result and accompanied by a warning that outcomes depend on transaction size, gas, and funding.

citations.quote: keep in mind that you could end up losing money with that amount when the gas fee are actually higher than the slippage profits
This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet
when you want to withdraw your funds, to stop the bot just hit the withdraw button pay the fees

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructions to install a wallet and fund a contract establish a workflow, but they do not establish deception. The funding passage expressly warns of losses, and the title's general money-making language does not erase that qualification. A reported result is also not the same as a guarantee: the speaker says the amount can vary with the initial funds and transaction conditions. The evidence therefore supports a risky technical example, not necessarily a dishonest solicitation.

citations.quote: you could end up losing money with that amount when the gas fee are actually higher than the slippage profits
you can actually increase it by using more initial fund to frontrun even higher transactions as well

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is narrow: it concerns gas fees exceeding slippage for a lower balance, not the possibility that the claimed bot or contract itself may fail or that the displayed return is unverified. The speaker still tells viewers to fund the contract, recommends at least one BNB, uses five BNB to maximize profit, and reports roughly 2.7 BNB in four hours. A limited cost caveat does not neutralize the central profit solicitation.

opening.argument: The video's observable structure is an operational walkthrough: it explains how to configure a wallet, add a network, open Remix, compile a contract, deploy it, and wait for confirmation. The supplied frames likewise show MetaMask setup and the Remix compiler and deployment interfaces. That is consistent with technology education or a demonstration of a blockchain workflow. Explaining how a tool is configured does not by itself certify the tool's performance or turn the lesson into a solicitation, especially where the speaker describes waiting for confirmations and later stopping and withdrawing.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference characterization focuses on the financial subject matter, but subject matter alone does not resolve the video's role. The narration spends substantial time on compiler, deployment, network, and confirmation steps, and the frames show the actual development interface. The speaker can be demonstrating a tool's claimed operation while leaving viewers to assess whether to use it. Technical instructions are not automatically a promise that the claimed returns will occur for every viewer.

citations.quote: choose the right compiler version in our case it's 0.6.6 plus commit
And now we need to wait for the transaction to be confirmed

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely neutral coding instruction. The workflow is explicitly tied to funding and operating a front-running bot, and the speaker directs viewers to put BNB into the contract before starting it. The claimed four-hour profit and advice to increase initial funds give the tutorial a promotional purpose. Showing a compiler or wallet interface demonstrates only that transactions were attempted, not that the system is legitimate or that the return claim is reliable.

citations.quote: Now, we need to top up our contract actually with funds so that we are able to actually, front run any transaction on the mempool
I recommend you guys as well also to check out my other videos especially the frontrun Ethereum version, the profits on that are just amazing right now

opening.argument: The supplied material does not show several features that would make the strongest scam characterization concrete. It does not request a password or recovery phrase, require recruitment, describe a downline, or promise a fixed return. Instead, it presents a user-operated contract with an explicit withdrawal control and transaction fees. The description also identifies the technical scope and provides code and deployment resources. On this record, the content can be read as promotion of a software workflow or service-like tool, with users retaining an operational withdrawal path, rather than proof of a concealed deposit-and-guaranteed-return scheme.

citations.quote: when you want to withdraw your funds, to stop the bot just hit the withdraw button pay the fees
Smart Contract Code
now we get the confirmation so basically that is the first step our bot is now running

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side calls the funding a scam mechanism, but funding a contract is not by itself proof that funds are secretly captured. The supplied instructions identify the amount, describe transaction fees, and expressly mention a withdrawal button. There is no shown request for private credentials or recruitment-based income. The technical mechanism may be unconventional, but unconventional trading automation is not automatically a fraudulent deposit scheme.

citations.quote: we are using as i said in our case 5 BNB to maximize our profit
when you want to withdraw your funds, to stop the bot just hit the withdraw button pay the fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a seed-phrase request or downline does not answer the actual allegation. The video instructs viewers to deploy code, top up the contract, pay fees, and start it, while claiming that it can front-run transactions and generate a large short-term return. A withdrawal button in the interface does not establish that withdrawals succeed or that the contract is safe. The code and links are merely supplied materials, not independent validation.
